database_summary: Sakila-like DVD rental schema in SQLite. Contains reference/dimensional tables (actor, category, language, country, city, address, store, staff), core transaction/event tables (rental, payment, inventory), catalog tables (film, film_text, film_actor, film_category) and customer. Row counts indicate small OLTP dataset (hundreds to tens of thousands). Foreign keys link customers/staff/stores/addresses to geography and staff, films to languages and categories via bridge tables, rentals/payments reference inventory, staff and customer. Many tables record last_update timestamps.

accepted.name: film_with_language_category
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.film_id,
  f.title,
  f.description,
  f.release_year,
  f.language_id,
  l.name AS name,
  f.original_language_id,
  f.rental_duration,
  f.rental_rate,
  f.length,
  f.replacement_cost,
  f.rating,
  f.special_features,
  fc.category_id,
  c.name AS category_name,
  f.last_update
FROM film f
LEFT JOIN language l ON f.language_id = l.language_id
LEFT JOIN film_category fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
LEFT JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
accepted.description: Denormalized film-level relation enriched with language and category names. One row per film-category (preserves film-category multiplicity). Useful as a starting point for catalog queries, counts by category/language, and joins to inventory/rental. | Use for: List films and their categories or languages; Aggregate film counts or average rental_rate by category or language; Filter films by category_name or language name

accepted.name: inventory_with_film_store
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.inventory_id,
  i.film_id,
  f.title AS title,
  i.store_id,
  s.address_id AS address_id,
  a.city_id AS city_id,
  ci.country_id AS country_id,
  ci.city AS city,
  co.country AS country,
  i.last_update
FROM inventory i
LEFT JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
LEFT JOIN store s ON i.store_id = s.store_id
LEFT JOIN address a ON s.address_id = a.address_id
LEFT JOIN city ci ON a.city_id = ci.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON ci.country_id = co.country_id
accepted.description: Inventory items joined to film and store/location info (via address -> city -> country). One row per inventory item. Useful for stock-levels, store-level availability, and joining to rental/payment events. | Use for: Which stores have which inventory items; Counts of inventory by store/city/country; Join inventory to rental/payment events for turnover analysis

accepted.name: customer_with_location
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.store_id,
  c.first_name,
  c.last_name,
  c.email,
  c.address_id,
  a.address AS address,
  a.address2 AS address2,
  a.district AS district,
  a.postal_code AS postal_code,
  a.phone AS phone,
  a.city_id AS city_id,
  ci.city AS city,
  ci.country_id AS country_id,
  co.country AS country,
  c.active,
  c.create_date,
  c.last_update
FROM customer c
LEFT JOIN address a ON c.address_id = a.address_id
LEFT JOIN city ci ON a.city_id = ci.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON ci.country_id = co.country_id
accepted.description: Customer rows enriched with address, city and country for geographic analysis. One row per customer. Useful for customer segmentation, regional reporting, and joins to payments/rentals. | Use for: Customer lists by city or country; Active vs inactive customer counts by region; Joining customers to payments and rentals for regional revenue

accepted.name: payments_by_customer_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.customer_id,
  COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count,
  SUM(p.amount) AS total_payment_amount,
  MIN(p.payment_date) AS first_payment_date,
  MAX(p.payment_date) AS last_payment_date
FROM payment p
GROUP BY p.customer_id
accepted.description: Aggregated payment measures per customer: total amount, payment_count, first and last payment dates. One row per customer. Useful for lifetime value, recency/frequency/monetary (RFM) analyses. | Use for: Customer lifetime value and revenue per customer; RFM segmentation using recency, frequency, monetary measures; Identify customers with no payments (LEFT JOIN against customer)

accepted.name: rentals_by_inventory_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.inventory_id,
  COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rental_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN r.return_date IS NOT NULL AND r.rental_date IS NOT NULL THEN
    (julianday(r.return_date) - julianday(r.rental_date))
    ELSE 0 END) AS total_rental_days,
  MIN(r.rental_date) AS first_rental_date,
  MAX(r.rental_date) AS last_rental_date
FROM rental r
GROUP BY r.inventory_id
accepted.description: Aggregated rental activity per inventory item: rental_count, total_rental_duration (in days, where return_date - rental_date), first and last rental dates. One row per inventory_id. Useful to measure item utilization and turnover. | Use for: Which inventory items are rented most often; Compute average rental duration per inventory or film; Identify unused inventory (rental_count = 0) by LEFT JOINing inventory

accepted.name: top_actors_by_film_count_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.actor_id,
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fa.film_id) AS actor_film_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT fa.film_id) DESC) AS actor_rank
FROM actor a
LEFT JOIN film_actor fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id
GROUP BY a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name
accepted.description: Actor-level ranking by number of distinct films an actor appears in. One row per actor with actor_film_count and actor_rank (dense). Useful for top-K actor queries and actor-based filtering. | Use for: Top-N actors by number of films; Filter actors by rank or count for reports

accepted.name: customer_payment_rfm
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.customer_id,
  p.payment_count,
  p.total_payment_amount,
  p.first_payment_date,
  p.last_payment_date,
  CASE WHEN p.last_payment_date IS NOT NULL THEN (julianday('now') - julianday(p.last_payment_date)) ELSE NULL END AS recency_days,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY p.total_payment_amount DESC) AS monetary_rank,
  SUM(p.total_payment_amount) OVER (ORDER BY p.total_payment_amount DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_revenue_ordered_by_monetary
FROM (
  SELECT
    p.customer_id,
    COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count,
    SUM(p.amount) AS total_payment_amount,
    MIN(p.payment_date) AS first_payment_date,
    MAX(p.payment_date) AS last_payment_date
  FROM payment p
  GROUP BY p.customer_id
) p
accepted.description: RFM-style measures with recency (days since last payment), frequency and monetary and running_total over customers ordered by total_payment_amount. One row per customer. Useful for segmentation and cumulative revenue analysis. | Use for: RFM segmentation and recency/frequency/monetary calculations; Cumulative revenue contribution by customers

accepted.name: latest_rental_per_inventory_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.rental_id,
  r.inventory_id,
  r.customer_id,
  r.rental_date,
  r.return_date,
  r.staff_id,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.inventory_id ORDER BY r.rental_date DESC) AS inventory_rental_rank
FROM rental r
accepted.description: For each inventory_id, the most recent rental (by rental_date). One row per inventory rental instance with per-inventory rank; downstream filters can select the latest (rank = 1). Useful for identifying current renter or most recent activity per item. | Use for: Find most recent rental per inventory item; Identify currently rented items (latest rental with NULL return_date)

accepted.name: staff_activity_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.staff_id,
  s.first_name,
  s.last_name,
  s.address_id,
  a.address AS address,
  a.city_id AS city_id,
  ci.city AS city,
  ci.country_id AS country_id,
  co.country AS country,
  s.email,
  s.store_id,
  s.active,
  s.username,
  s.last_update
FROM staff s
LEFT JOIN address a ON s.address_id = a.address_id
LEFT JOIN city ci ON a.city_id = ci.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON ci.country_id = co.country_id
accepted.description: Staff members with their store and address/city/country context. One row per staff. Useful for staff performance joins to rentals/payments and regional staffing reports. | Use for: Staff lists by region or store; Join staff to rentals/payments for performance metrics

accepted.name: film_length_and_rate_norm
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.film_id,
  f.title,
  f.description,
  CASE WHEN f.release_year = '' THEN NULL ELSE f.release_year END AS release_year,
  f.language_id,
  f.rental_duration,
  CAST(f.rental_rate AS NUMERIC) AS rental_rate,
  CAST(f.length AS NUMERIC) AS length,
  CAST(f.replacement_cost AS NUMERIC) AS replacement_cost,
  CASE WHEN CAST(f.length AS NUMERIC) > 0 THEN (CAST(f.replacement_cost AS NUMERIC) / CAST(f.length AS NUMERIC)) ELSE NULL END AS cost_per_minute,
  f.rating,
  f.special_features,
  f.last_update
FROM film f
accepted.description: Normalized film attributes with canonical numeric casts and a derived length_minutes and cost_per_minute. One row per film. Useful for numeric comparisons and filters on film length and rates. | Use for: Compare films by length or rental_rate; Filter films by cost_per_minute or length thresholds; Compute aggregates like average length or average rental_rate
